description: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of queries used during inference and the MRR@10 metric for different query selection strategies. The x-axis is labeled “Number of queries used during inference (S.)” and has a linear scale ranging from 1 to 10, with tick labels at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled “MRR@10” and has a linear scale ranging from 33.0 to 36.5, with tick labels at intervals of 0.5. There are five lines displayed: a black dashed line representing “DPR w/o query” which starts at approximately 35.3 at S=1, declines to 35.1 at S=10; a green solid line representing “DPR w/ gold” which starts at approximately 34.1 at S=1 and increases to 34.8 at S=10; a purple solid line representing “DPR w/ top-1” which starts at approximately 34.9 at S=1 and increases to 36.1 at S=10; a blue dashed line representing “DPR w/ random” which starts at approximately 35.1 at S=1 and declines to 35.0 at S=10; and an orange solid line representing “DPR w/ curriculum” which starts at approximately 33.3 at S=1 and increases to 36.0 at S=10.
caption_used: Comparison of different query selection strategies. During training, we first expand the document with a query selected from the generated queries using a specific strategy, and then train DPR with the expanded document. During inference, we evaluate the well-trained DPR retrievers with corpus expansion (solid lines) and the typical representation (dotted lines) on the dev set of MS-Marco, where the solid and dotted lines with the same color are results for the same DPR. Notably, the 'DPR w/ bottom-1' strategy demonstrates a consistent increase in MRR@10, reaching approximately 35.2 at S=10, surpassing the 'DPR w/ random' strategy. Additionally, the 'DPR w/ gold' strategy shows a slower rate of improvement compared to 'DPR w/ top-1', stabilizing at around 34.8 by S=10. The 'DPR w/ curriculum' strategy consistently exceeds the performance of 'DPR w/ random' across all query counts, with a peak MRR@10 of approximately 36.0 at S=10.
